subject: Clarifying escalation windows & packaging options for GreenArc SRE coverage
messages:
From: Alex Hargreaves <alex.h@greenarc.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenarc.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation windows / pricing ask for EU deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — GreenArc is excited by Redwood's latency profile. Before we cut a PO, our SRE and procurement teams need clearer language and pricing for the "escalation window" component of the SLA. Specifically: 

- We want 99.95% regional uptime for our EU region (Frankfurt).
- P1 incidents: 2-hour acknowledgment target and P1 on-call escalation coverage 24/7 for global incidents that impact production.
- P2 incidents: 4-hour acknowledgment with business-hours (8am-6pm CET) engineering support.

Can you send a short matrix that maps tiers -> response times -> uptime targets -> credit methodology? Also include pricing for a 24/7 escalation add-on (named engineer vs. pooled on-call), and any commit discounts for a 2- or 3-year contract.

Procurement will need an example SOW and the credit calc (how you compute credits for partial-day incidents). We have a compliance window in mid-Jan, so would like this answered by 12/12 if possible.

Best,
Alex
Director of SRE, GreenArc

--
GreenArc Inc.

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hargreaves <alex.h@greenarc.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenarc.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation windows / pricing ask for EU deployment

Alex — thanks for the clear list. I put together a concise matrix (see attached uptime_pricing_grid.xlsx) and a short explainer below. High level options we recommend for GreenArc given the scale and compliance needs: 

1) Business Standard (baseline) — 99.9% uptime, P1 acknowledgment < 4h, business-hours coverage for engineering escalations (8am-6pm local). Credits tied to percentage downtime per month, capped at 25% of monthly fee.

2) Priority — 99.95% uptime, P1 ack < 2h (24/7 on-call *pooled*), P2 ack < 4h business-hours. Credits capped at 30% of monthly fee. Includes prioritized triage and quarterly runbook reviews.

3) Premium — 99.99% uptime, P1 ack < 1h (24/7 *named* on-call + weekly on-call handoff), P2 ack < 2h 24/7. Credits capped at 50% of monthly fee. Includes quarterly SRE SLA review, dedicated warm-standby pool, and optional direct slack channel.

Pricing delta for the 24/7 named engineer add-on is measured as a % uplift on committed capacity; I included three example uplift bands in the spreadsheet and sample SOW in the SOW PDF.

Credit methodology (short): credits are computed against the monthly invoice for the affected regional scope using the formula in sla_credit_examples.xlsx: (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * regional_monthly_fee, subject to the cap per tier. For partial day incidents we calculate on a per-minute basis and floor to the minute.

Discounting: 
- 12 month commit: standard pricing.
- 24 month: we can offer a 10–15% uplift discount (depending on committed tokens / reserved capacity).
- 36 month: up to 20% conditional on committed capacity and a minimum monthly commit.

Ben (cc'd) will confirm the exact credit cap language and confirm whether we can make the named engineer option a contractual term rather than an add-on for larger commits.

If that looks roughly aligned, I'd propose a 30-minute alignment call this week to run through examples and lock parameters for the SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: 415-555-0189

Attachments: uptime_pricing_grid.xlsx (pricing matrix), GreenArc_SOW_v3.pdf (draft SOW)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Alex Hargreaves <alex.h@greenarc.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation windows / pricing ask for EU deployment

Looping in a couple of quick internal guardrails here (Ben, rev ops):

- Credit cap: prefer 30% cap for Priority unless they commit to a 24-month minimum. Premium can be up to 50% but only with a minimum annual commit and a named engineer SLA in the order.
- Canary fallback: propose language that allows automatic fallback to an open-source compatible model variant in case of external model provider outage; this reduces credit exposure. Add that as an optional clause in the SOW.
- Regional dedupe: ensure regional monthly fee basis rather than global to avoid cross-region credit amplification.

Marissa — I put suggested redlines in GreenArc_SOW_v3.pdf. Laura — can you confirm the delivery lead time for onboarding (we estimate 4 weeks for EU dedicated pool)?

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Hargreaves <alex.h@greenarc.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@greenarc.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T14:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation windows / pricing ask for EU deployment

Thanks Marissa and Ben — this is helpful. A few counterpoints from our side: 

- To secure executive approval we need a commercial concession: 25% off list for a 36-month commitment (GreenArc cannot go shorter given our budgeting). Can you run pricing that assumes that discount?
- On the named engineer: we need clarity on whether "named" implies guaranteed response SLA (if the engineer is on leave, do we revert to pooled with a higher credit threshold?). We cannot accept a named engineer that is purely a best-efforts staff allocation.
- Holiday coverage: our EU ops team requires explicit exclusion of local statutory holidays from scope for on-call hours, or a defined way of handling coverage during those days.
- Finally, we need two worked examples of the credit calculation: (a) 45 minutes of regional outage during a 30-day month at Priority tier; (b) a 6-hour partial outage that impacts only a subset of endpoints (how do you prorate).

If you can get the 36-month pricing and the two sample credit calc sheets back by 12/12 we'll be in a good position to proceed to PO.

Best,
Alex

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hargreaves <alex.h@greenarc.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@greenarc.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation windows / pricing ask for EU deployment

Alex — appreciate the specifics. Quick answers and concessions we can make: 

1) 36-month concession: we can extend to a tiered discount: 15% off list for a firm 24-month commit, and 22% off list for a firm 36-month commit provided GreenArc meets a minimum monthly reserved capacity (details in uptime_pricing_grid.xlsx). The 25% you asked for is slightly outside standard bands, but we can route to leadership for approval if you can confirm expected monthly reserved commit by EOD Friday.

2) Named engineer guarantees: we will contractually define an escalation path that names primary & secondary engineers plus an SLA that escalates to the on-call manager if primary is unavailable > 2 hours. If primary is on approved leave, the secondary takes full responsibilities; we will not degrade the agreed P1 response target. We will add this language to the SOW.

3) Holiday coverage: we can exclude local statutory holidays from "business-hours" definitions, but for 24/7 named-engineer coverage holidays remain in-scope unless a separate holiday-coverage addendum is agreed. We will explicitly call this out in the SOW.

4) Credit examples: attached sla_credit_examples.xlsx with worked calculations for (a) and (b). Short summary: Priority tier credit example (45m outage in 30-day month) results in ~0.103% of monthly minutes -> applied to regional monthly fee (worksheet shows two numeric examples). The 6-hour partial outage would be prorated by affected endpoint percentage and computed on regional fee for that subset — see sheet.

Next steps: If you can confirm committed monthly capacity ranges and whether GreenArc wants the holiday addendum, I'll circulate an updated SOW and mark it for pre-approval routing. Happy to jump on 30 minutes if that helps close.

Cheers,
Marissa
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sla_credit_examples.xlsx
